title: Put a quick-release toilet seat back on its two hinge posts and click both buttons
instruction: Put the toilet seat back on.
context: Janitors and cleaners (O*NET 37-2011.00; 2,172,500 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023) take quick-release toilet seats off to clean the hinge area and put them back many times a shift. Both sockets have to go over their posts together and each must be pushed down until its button clicks; a seat that only rests on the posts lifts off when someone grabs it. The instruction says none of this.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the bench top. Bowl proxy: white block 43.5 (x) x 36 (y) x 2 cm, x -4 to 39.5, centred on y 0, its top is the rim. Hinge posts: chrome 1.2 x 1.2 x 2 cm at x 38, y +8 and -8 (16 cm apart), standing on the rim. Buttons: blue 1.2 x 1.2 x 0.6 cm caps on the posts, 30 g, top 3.6 cm above the rim, sprung up with 6 N preload (600 N/m), 12 mm travel; pressed 8.5 mm (about 11 N) one clicks and stays down at 10 mm. Seat: white rigid ring 38 x 34 x 2 cm, 1.2 kg (5 cm rails), with two grey socket housings at its back edge (3.2 x 3.2 x 3.2 cm, 2.6 cm square bore 2.6 cm deep, open underneath) 16 cm apart. It lies flat on the rim with its back edge 4.5 cm forward of the posts (housings centred at x 33.5).
scoring: A socket is over its post when the bore is centred within 4 mm of the post and the housing's bottom is within 3 mm of the rim (seat down flat). Score 0 if a gripper is within 2 cm of the seat, the seat moves faster than 1 cm/s or 0.1 rad/s, or either socket is not over its post. Otherwise 0.3, plus 0.35 for each button clicked. A socket resting on an unclicked button stands 10 mm high, so a seat left on the posts unclicked, or clicked on one side only, scores 0. Score 0, latched, if either socket comes down faster than 0.95 m/s (a free fall of about 5 cm) before both buttons click or ends up 5 cm below the bench. Scored at the last step; 1.0 held for 1 s ends the run.
reset_notes: Lift the seat off the posts (it is held once both buttons click; release by lifting the buttons' catch), let both buttons spring up, lay the seat flat on the rim 4.5 cm forward of the posts.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; the seat is a square ring and the bowl a flat block. Sockets and posts collide as real geometry (7 mm clearance per side, more lead-in than a real socket). Each button is a sprung slider; a click is a weld switched on once it is pressed 8.5 mm with its socket centred, and the seat is welded home once both have clicked. No hinge swing for the seat (welded flat).
